text:
rahul.s: noticed a weird uptick in S3 reads from the ingest pipeline after yesterday's RBAC refactor, looks like the ephemeral SA got broader perms :thinking_face:
liz.h: ugh, can you paste the object keys or policy we’re seeing?
rahul.s: logs show GetObject on customer-prod-bucket from ingest-processor-sa at 16:12 UTC, should only have access to ingest-temp/* 
mike_t: did the roles->groups mapping change in the last deploy? iirc we flattened a few bindings into 'data-processing' group
rahul.s: yeah the PR consolidated role attachments. suspect a merge accidentally kept an older binding: `allow: s3:GetObject resource: arn:aws:s3:::customer-prod-bucket/*`
liz.h: ok immediate steps: 1) revoke the ephemeral credentials, 2) remove inadvertent binding, 3) run audit to list any other SAs with prod access. can someone revoke tokens?
oncall-bot: automated action: created incident INC-2026-042, assigned to eng-security. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/sa-privilege-leak
mike_t: i can revoke the ephemeral token and patch the role binding now. command i'll run: 
```
# revoke token
aws sts revoke-access-key --access-key-id AKIA... 
# remove binding
rbacctl remove-binding --group data-processing --role s3-prod-reader
```
dina-sec: also rotate the KMS CMK grant if any service had a direct grant; quick check: `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/customer-prod`
rahul.s: confirmed there is one grant issued to `ingest-processor-sa` at 2026-03-22T15:58Z. please revoke the grant too.
mike_t: revoking grant now and removing binding, will push a canary change to ensure no other groups picked up the binding.
liz.h: while mike does that i'll add a temporary deny policy on customer-prod-bucket for all pipeline SAs as a belt-and-suspenders measure: 
```
# put bucket policy deny for pipeline role prefix
aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket customer-prod-bucket --policy file://deny-pipeline-temp.json
```
rahul.s: thanks. after revoke + deny, let's run a search for any read events from other SAs in the last 24h and collect principals. i'll export CloudTrail.
oncall-bot: action required: exclude the deny policy from the maintenance window 02:00-03:00 UTC, noted in incident.
mike_t: done: binding removed, KMS grant revoked, ephemeral creds invalidated. pushed ACL change and created PR to fix role->group mapping (PR #4523).
dina-sec: i ran `aws kms list-grants` and confirmed grant is gone. starting an audit query: `SELECT eventTime, userIdentity.principalId, eventName FROM cloudtrail WHERE eventName='GetObject' AND eventTime > '2026-03-21T00:00:00Z'`
liz.h: audit results?
rahul.s: looks like only three GetObject hits from ingest-processor-sa during the window. no other SAs found. i exported principals and flagged them in INC-2026-042.
dina-sec: recommend follow-ups: 1) add a unit test in rbac-sync to catch wildcard merges, 2) add an alert on sudden spike of prod-bucket reads from non-prod namespaces, 3) add KMS grant verification during role binding merges.
mike_t: agreed. i'll include the rbac-sync test in PR #4523 and open a follow-up ticket to improve merge-time checks.
liz.h: closing immediate incident actions: deny policy will remain for 4 hours, then we'll replace with least-privilege rule once CI tests pass. assign to engineering for postmortem.
rahul.s: thanks all — going to notify customers we rotated credentials and there was no data exfil detected. will post summary in the incident and follow up with postmortem doc. :lock: :thumbsup:
